title: Public Sector
meta: Process improvement and KPIs for Canadian public sector organizations: improve productivity, meet service standards and get more value from every budget dollar.
h1: Deliver better public services with efficient processes and KPIs
lead: We help public sector organizations improve productivity and service delivery while controlling operating and capital costs. We work with your staff and union so improvements are practical and they last.
intro: How do you deliver more for citizens within the same budget?

Public sector organizations are asked to grow services and maintain infrastructure while operating and capital budgets stay tight. Real improvement takes more than a boardroom conversation. We work directly with your managers, frontline staff and union representatives in ways that are relatable and respectful. Together we map how services are delivered today, define key performance measures that link daily work to your service standards, and remove steps that add no value for citizens. We act as your coaches in performance improvement, building a culture of continuous improvement and accountability that continues long after the project is complete.
signs: Service standards are set but rarely measured or reported
Backlogs and processing times grow faster than staffing
Requests pass through many approvals and handoffs
Capital projects are proposed to fix problems that may be process issues
Staff are stretched, and past improvement efforts did not stick
challenges: Demand for services and infrastructure keeps rising while operating and capital budgets remain constrained.
Without clear KPIs it is hard to show citizens, councils or boards how services are performing and where resources are needed.
Processes that cross departments accumulate steps, waiting time and rework that citizens experience as delays.
Sustaining change in a unionized workplace
Improvements succeed only when staff and the union are involved early and see the changes as fair and practical.
services: We define measures for service levels, productivity, speed and quality on key processes, so you can report performance and track improvement against your baseline.
Review of current practices and tools
We map key processes, analyze financial and operating data, observe work directly and document current management tools.
We observe service delivery to separate work that adds value for citizens from waiting, duplicate approvals and rework, revealing capacity.
We collaborate with your team and union in relatable ways, so your people are the key drivers of the change.
We assess change readiness, then build a practical change plan with clear communication and training.
We work with leadership to implement tools that turn your strategic plan into activities every employee understands, such as visual boards and regular performance reviews.

figs.title: A permit application, start to finish
figs.caption: A swim lane view of a permit process. Watch applications wait at department reviews, then click Fix the bottleneck.

steps.label: Submit application
steps.text: The applicant submits the application and drawings.

steps.label: Log and check intake
steps.text: Intake staff log the file and take the fee.

steps.label: Initial screening
steps.text: A planner screens the application against zoning and policy.

steps.label: Department reviews
steps.text: Engineering, fire and other departments review one after another, each with its own queue.

steps.label: Request missing info
steps.text: Reviewers find missing information. The file goes back to the applicant, then rejoins the review queue.

steps.label: Make the decision
steps.text: The approving manager signs off on the decision.

steps.label: Issue notification
steps.text: Intake staff issue the permit or the decision letter.

steps.label: Receive permit
steps.text: The applicant receives the permit and can start work.

before: Files sent back for missing info

config.fix_title: Fixed: parallel reviews and a completeness checklist
config.fix_text: A completeness checklist at intake stops incomplete files entering review, departments review in parallel against service standards, and applicants can see where their file is. Waiting time drops and fewer files are sent back.

examples: Permit processing at a mid-sized municipality
applications moved through departments one after another, and incomplete files were sent back late in the process.
a completeness check at intake and parallel reviews shortened processing times and reduced resubmissions.
Work orders in a public works yard
crews waited for materials and equipment at the start of each job, and work orders were tracked on paper.
next-day job kitting and a simple digital work order board reduced waiting and made backlogs visible.
Front-counter service at a regional agency
citizens waited in one line regardless of request type, and simple requests took as long as complex ones.
triage at arrival and online options for routine requests cut wait times and freed staff for complex cases.
outcomes: KPIs and service standards measured and reported consistently
Improved productivity and shorter processing times, tracked against your baseline
Lower operating costs and capital spending deferred where process fixes are enough
Fewer handoffs, approvals and rework in key services
Staff and union engaged as drivers of the change
A culture of continuous improvement and accountability

faq: How do you work with unions?

We involve union representatives early, explain the purpose of observations and focus on removing obstacles to good work rather than on individual performance. Staff help design the changes, which builds trust and makes them last.
How is ROI measured in a public sector context?
Before the project starts we agree measures with you, such as processing time, cost per transaction, backlog size, overtime or capital spending avoided. Results are tracked against your own baseline.
Can you help us report on service standards?
Yes. We help define KPIs tied to your service standards and set up simple reporting so councils, boards and citizens can see how services are performing.
Do you work with municipalities as well as provincial agencies?
Yes. Our approach suits municipalities, regional districts, provincial agencies and other public institutions, and we follow your procurement and privacy requirements.
